Rachel L: BankEdge wants a short POC to validate streaming SDK + function calls behind Okta and their corporate proxy. Need SSO flow, batching tips for low p95, reserved-capacity pricing for ~200 qps, and a tiny Go adapter. Anyone own?

Ben K: I'll take SSO/proxy. We support SP-initiated SAML with Okta. For proxies that terminate TLS we need their CA bundle and egress IPs. Recommend ephemeral token exchange via backend to avoid long-lived client creds.

Sam P: Batching notes: for <100ms p95 use continuous batching with max_batch_latency=10ms and max_batch_size=32 for typical 4k token prompts. For cost-first, try 25ms + size 128 (~15% token cost reduction). Suggest KV prefix caching. I'll add a micro-benchmark to the runbook.

Olivia C: Pricing ask: 200 qps sustained. Need 1yr vs 3yr committed options and a suggested GPU reserve.

Ben K: Thumb estimate: 3-5 A100-equivalents with 20% headroom and autoscale for bursts; exact quote from finance.

Presales Bot: Runbook created -> https://console.redwood.ai/runbooks/presales/bankedge-poc-checklist (items: Okta metadata, proxy CA, network egress, Go sample).

Rachel L: Can someone paste a one-page Go snippet for ephemeral token exchange + starting a streaming session with function calls? Bank's infra team wants it.

Sam P: Tiny Go sketch:
```go
// exchange ephemeral token
resp, _ := http.Post("https://auth.redwood.ai/v1/ephemeral", "application/json", bytes.NewBuffer(body))
tok, _ := io.ReadAll(resp.Body)
// start SSE stream
req, _ := http.NewRequest("GET", "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=rwd-medium&functions=1", nil)
req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+string(tok))
client := &http.Client{}
res, _ := client.Do(req)
// read SSE events from res.Body
```
Full sample repo in runbook.

Ben K: Next steps: Rachel collects Okta metadata + proxy CA; Sam posts bench + cost calc; Olivia prepares pricing sheet. Follow-up 24h.
